source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source_reported_historical_synonyms: Psoralea latestipulata Shinners (historical basionym of species; shown under var. latestipulatum)

morphology_source_reported.leaves: Leaflets usually elliptic to oblanceolate, 5–15 mm wide; leaves and fruits gland-dotted
morphology_source_reported.flowers: 18–26 mm long, blue, lavender or purple petals
morphology_source_reported.variety_diagnostics: Var. appressum with appressed stem hairs; var. latestipulatum with erect stem hairs; Flora calls pubescence the only consistent distinction

additional_key_characters.peduncles: Shorter than or equal to subtending petioles [species branch key p. 683]
additional_key_characters.stipules: Usually 2.5–7 mm wide, elliptic-lanceolate to falcate-oblanceolate or orbicular [key p. 683]
additional_key_characters.inflorescence: Dense spike-like racemes 2–4 cm thick [key p. 683]

cautions: Flora states other size characters overlap between varieties; do not generalize varietal pubescence as a species-wide state
Historical taxon concept requires reconciliation before identification-scoring use
Regional habitat does not establish local BONAP nativity

Internal key ambiguity: printed p. 683 also places species at a branch describing spreading pilose stems, but p. 686 explicitly differentiates var. appressum from var. latestipulatum based on appressed vs erect hairs; key must not override variety-specific treatment.
Do not treat key characters from different decision paths as simultaneously obligatory until rechecked.
